messages:
maria: quick sync  deciding where to place retry/backoff logic for paginated list calls. two options: transport-level safe retries vs iterator-level retries. pros/cons?

kevin: transport-level keeps iterator code tiny but hides replays. if the server side has non-idempotent behavior on page fetch we could double-execute things. need a dedupe story.

ali: runtime idea: add a light resume handshake. transport attaches x-request-nonce and accepts x-resume-token returned by server. that lets server detect duplicate FetchPage(cursor) attempts and return stable pages. safer for transport retries.

sophie: UX note: languages differ (py generator, ts async-iter, go channel). we have to guarantee same observable semantics for "at-most-once" vs "at-least-once" delivery and final error handling. docs must be explicit.

ci-bot: failing test: pagination-resume-spec on macOS, logs: https://ci.internal/runs/5522 :mag:

kevin: concrete Go sketch to discuss semantics:

```
// Go
for p := range client.List(ctx, req) {
  for _, itm := range p.Items {
    process(itm)
  }
}
```

kevin: If transport retries a FetchPage and server yields overlapping items for safety, caller could see duplicates. Resume-token approach can avoid overlap if semantics defined.

maria: suggestion: default mode = transport-safe-retry for unary page RPCs, where transport will retry transient errors only when resume-token is present or when the call is marked idempotent. fallback to surface-retry if caller sets retry_mode="surface".

ali: runtime tasks: add header hooks x-request-nonce + x-resume-token; expose a hook so server teams can opt into dedupe via nonce+cursor. Add server-side doc with recommended behavior for returning next_resume_token.

kevin: sdk tasks: expose iterator config: retry_mode enum {"transport","surface","none"}, backoff settings, and expose last_resume_token on the iterator/error so users can resume after failure. I'll draft TS/Go/Python shapes.

sophie: docs tasks: write canonical examples showing how to opt-out, how to handle side-effects safely (idempotency tokens or moving side-effects to consumer after ack). Also add a note differentiating stream reconnection (no auto-retries) vs page fetch retries.

maria: important: streaming RPCs should NOT use transport automatic retries because re-establishing a stream has ordering and continuity implications. those should be handled by surface logic that knows how to re-subscribe and reconcile.

kevin: tests we need:
- transient network drop mid-iteration: default transport mode should resume from server next_resume_token and avoid duplicates
- when retry_mode=surface, iterator must bubble the error for user retrying with explicit resume token
- behavior when server does not support resume-token: transport must degrade to surface-retry semantics (bubble error)

ali: agree. runtime will include a toggle to emit x-request-nonce for outgoing page calls so we can opt servers in gradually.

maria: error model: iterator should return a consistent error class across SDKs with fields: cause_message, transient(boolean), last_resume_token(string|empty). unify in docs.

sophie: I'll draft docs pages and example snippets. want to call out migration guidance: servers should start returning resume_token even if no dedupe implemented. that allows clients to opt-in incrementally.

ci-bot: note: flaky integration test ticket created: PAG-1123.

kevin: timeline: I'll ship iterator API PR (TS + Go + Py interface) by next Tue. ali: runtime change window next week?

ali: yes, will schedule header hook and docs in the runtime repo for the next deploy. will include compatibility flag.

maria: great. i'll capture this as RFC follow-up with explicit decision: default transport-safe-retry for unary pagination when resume-token or idempotent flag present; surface-mode opt-out; streams never auto-retry. meeting to reconvene after PRs land. :thumbsup:
